patch_description: The metrics show cost decreases monotonically as spreading is reduced: the load-aware spreading program (1005.13) is best so far, but earlier pure cost-first variants with less spreading got close (1035–1065). The recommendation is to go fully cost-first: for each destination, generate up to k=4 candidate paths via k-shortest-path enumeration (with Dijkstra fallback) and assign ALL partitions to the single cheapest path. Any spreading across parallel routes adds extra per-partition transfer cost without reducing total cost, so candidate generation is kept purely for robustness. This retains the structural advantages (k-shortest candidates, Dijkstra fallback, safe unreachable handling) while removing all load-based spreading that increased cost.
